copy.blurb:
FIFA World Cup 2026 on Sunday, overnight UTC kickoff, brings Jordan and Argentina together. The Desk's read disagrees with the market on the Argentina side, by +5.4pp — and that disagreement is the Pick.

On Elo, Argentina comes in 610 points ahead — Jordan at 1530, Argentina at 2140. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. No host, home-ground, or altitude adjustments apply here; the prior reads straight from Elo.

Three-way split from the model: Jordan to win at 3%, the draw at 10%, and Argentina to win at 87%. The away side reads 87% on this distribution — the model's central case for Argentina.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: Jordan to win at 4%, the draw at 12%, and Argentina to win at 82%. Reading those three numbers as a probability distribution, the market's view is internally consistent. The disagreement with the model is concentrated on the Argentina side — 82% on the market, 87% on the engine, a +5.4pp gap.

The +3pp Pick threshold isn't on the point estimate, it's on the 5th-percentile from a 100-sample bootstrap of the Elo prior plus bonuses. On Argentina, that haircut lands the model at 86%; the market is at 82%. Even on the conservative reading, the gap is +4.3pp. The point is selection, not a blanket call. Most matches the model and the market agree on. This is one of the ones where they don't, and the gap is on the Argentina side specifically.

What would close this gap: confirmed team news that pulls the prior down on the side we like, a venue or weather change, or a tournament suspension landing before kickoff. With kickoff 36 days out, the refresh is weekly until we cross five days, then daily, then hourly inside the final day. A Pick this wide doesn't collapse on small news; a narrow one can flip to Pass on a single refresh. Either way, the engine republishes and the page reflects the latest read.
drivers: This is a selection call on the Argentina side, not a blanket read on the market.
Confirmed XI, fitness news, and weather re-enter the prior closer to kickoff.
Bootstrap lower-bound on the Argentina side still clears the Pick threshold.
Editorial analysis only — Odds Primer does not place trades or recommend a wager.

editorial_citations.quote: Argentina will hope to defend their title from 2022 after following it up with the Copa América in 2024.

copy.summary: On Argentina, the model is +5.4pp out from Polymarket. Our number reads 87%; the market reads 82%. That gap is the basis for the Pick.
copy.title: Jordan v Argentina · the model leans Argentina
